prTitle: feat(uptime): Add ability to use queues to manage parallelism
head: 9966ec5a13e331659c3ea00981f9b11b0faf821f

prOriginalConhecido.nota: Found by title search (branch danf/uptime-queue-consumer). Benchmark head 9966ec5a is the PR's last commit; same 7 files. Squash-merged as 33f4fddf.

tps.bug: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.terminate signals the commit thread without joining it, so the background thread is claimed to keep committing offsets for revoked partitions after terminate.
tps.evidenciaOpus: terminate() sets shutdown_event (queue_consumer.py:340-342), so _commit_loop exits after at most the iteration in progress; it does not keep committing. Any exception there is caught and logged. Not joining is consistent with terminate being the immediate, non-blocking shutdown, whereas close() is the graceful path that joins.
tps.evidenciaAstra: The newly added terminate() signals shutdown but never joins the commit thread (src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:340-342). The loop does not recheck shutdown after wait(), so an in-flight iteration can retrieve offsets and call commit_function after terminate() returns and partitions are revoked (queue_consumer.py:274-287). It eventually exits, but the missing synchronization creates a real late-commit race.
